title: Development of an Intelligent CRM Platform with Automated Customer Interaction Analysis
papers: DialogSum: A Real-Life Scenario Dialogue Summarization Dataset
Labelled dialogue summaries and benchmark experiments expose discourse and coreference challenges.
English everyday dialogues differ from customer records and local business vocabulary.
Use public dialogues for a smoke benchmark, then evaluate a separate domain set.
QMSum: A New Benchmark for Query-based Multi-domain Meeting Summarization
Locate-then-summarise connects requested information to relevant dialogue spans.
Long meetings and query-focused summaries do not directly represent short CRM interactions.
Retain source turn identifiers for every extracted fact and inspect evidence during review.
DialSummEval: Revisiting Summarization Evaluation for Dialogues
Compares automatic metrics against human judgements on coherence, consistency, fluency and relevance.
Findings depend on the studied datasets and model outputs; one metric cannot establish business utility.
Combine human factuality and key-fact coverage with timing measurements, rather than relying on ROUGE alone.
Analyzing and Evaluating Faithfulness in Dialogue Summarization
Analyses factual errors and proposes FacEval with transformed multiple-choice questions.
The paper notes that rule-based transformations cover only designed error types.
Add speaker swaps, negation changes and unsupported commitments to the error test set.
SummaC: Re-Visiting NLI-based Models for Inconsistency Detection in Summarization
Segments source and summary into smaller units and aggregates entailment signals.
An NLI score on summarisation benchmarks does not certify a CRM statement as true.
Consider consistency scoring as a secondary experiment, with human adjudication for the main outcome.
Annotating and Detecting Fine-grained Factual Errors for Dialogue Summarization
DIASUMFACT supplies fine-grained factual error annotations and compares error detectors.
The authors report limitations in practical error detection and evaluate their method on that dataset.
Use an explicit error taxonomy and retain reviewer decisions rather than automatically approving analyses.
GPT-Calls: Enhancing Call Segmentation and Tagging by Generating Synthetic Conversations via Large Language Models
Uses topic anchors and synthetic conversations to support call segmentation and tagging.
Production and domain-specific evidence cannot be reproduced from our small prototype; synthetic data are not user validation.
Compare topic tagging against a keyword baseline. Label synthetic fixtures separately from field evidence.
Exploring the Factual Consistency in Dialogue Comprehension of Large Language Models
Evaluates dialogue summaries and factual question answering, including participant attribution errors.
Results concern the evaluated model versions and data; published error rates are not predictions for this project.
Test attribution, dates and next steps on held-out interactions. Record model and prompt versions.
FineSurE: Fine-grained Summarization Evaluation using LLMs
Evaluates faithfulness, completeness and conciseness through fact checks and key-fact alignment.
The main benchmark is news, and LLM judging introduces domain and evaluator dependence.
Adopt key-fact coverage as a human rubric. Treat an automated judge as secondary and never as sole ground truth.
Factual Dialogue Summarization via Learning from Large Language Models
Distils generated positive and negative examples to improve smaller dialogue summarisation models.
Training requires data and compute; benchmark improvements do not prove multilingual CRM readiness.
Keep fine-tuning outside the mandatory MVP. Compare a pretrained model with the extractive baseline first.

tech: Proposed: Vue. Vue experience was reported by Beybit. Components, forms and a review workspace fit the scope [T01–T03].
Do not claim a performance advantage without measurement. Prototype is portable HTML/JS, not a completed Vue application.
Proposed: FastAPI for validated API contracts and proximity to Python analysis code [T04–T06].
Danial must confirm maintainability. Keep inference outside request handlers. This is a documented proposal, not a benchmark winner.
Proposed: relational customer/review records with JSONB analysis payloads [T07–T09].
MongoDB supports transactions. SQLite remains suitable for some embedded cases. Actual multi-user write and backup needs drive selection.
Proposed: HTTP JSON for UI/API and durable PostgreSQL job state for the worker. It minimises initial services [T10, T11, T14].
GraphQL query flexibility and a broker may be useful later. Queue retries, leases and idempotency still need implementation and tests.
Deterministic extractive baseline plus one pretrained candidate
Mandatory baseline is inspectable and cheap. Compare a locally runnable pretrained method before choosing the final approach [L03–L10, T12, T13].
The final model is deliberately unselected until quality, language, licence, latency and hardware tests. Do not silently send client records to an external provider.
requirements: An analyst can view only assigned customer records; a manager can view all records in this organisation; only an admin manages users. Anonymous and forbidden requests return 401/403 without object content.
API access matrix including direct-ID requests
Authorised users create, view and update a customer with a unique ID, display name and owner. Blank names fail validation and rejected updates leave stored data unchanged.

Enter or import JSON with customer ID, channel, timestamp and ordered speaker/text turns. Unknown customer, invalid timestamp, missing turn text and excess size produce per-record errors before persistence.
Search by customer name and filter interactions by customer, channel, date and review state. Combining filters returns their intersection and shows a usable empty state.
API query tests and UI task

For the same interaction revision and method/config version, repeated creation requests return one job. Status is queued, running, succeeded or failed. Bounded retry never overwrites a successful run.
Duplicate submission, worker crash and retry tests
A completed run stores topic labels, an at-most-120-word summary, source-turn references, source hash, method/model/config version and creation time. Invalid references fail output validation.
A reviewer inspects source and result side by side, edits the reviewed summary and approves or rejects it. The original output remains immutable and reviewer, timestamp and decision are recorded.
Failed jobs show an actionable error without customer text or secrets in the message. An authorised retry creates an attempt record and preserves prior failure history.
Timeout, unavailable model and malformed-output tests
Authorised export returns only accessible customer/interactions, both raw and reviewed results, provenance and review status. Empty selection produces a clear validation message.
An experiment records dataset revision, baseline/candidate, configuration and metrics. An output table separates measured results from unexecuted targets.
Re-run using frozen inputs and manifest
A manager sees counts by topic and review state from the same authorised filtered data. Counts reconcile with the underlying list.
A second connector is added only after mandatory scenarios pass and data permission is documented.
nfr: No secrets or real customer records in Git. Example configuration uses placeholders. External inference stays disabled unless a data-use decision permits it.
Core review/import tasks work with keyboard only. Controls have labels and visible focus. At 390 px and 1440 px the primary workflow has no unintended page overflow.
Manual keyboard pass and browser checks

On a documented 4-core/8-GB reference host and 10 concurrent users over 1,000 synthetic customers and 5,000 interactions, non-inference reads target p95 <= 500 ms over 200 requests after warm-up. Exclude network-to-model time and report it separately.
Load test with recorded host and request mix; target, not observed result

With fixed model, host and inputs up to 2,000 words, report cold/warm p50/p95 latency, memory and failure rate. Set a 60-second job timeout and at most 2 automatic retries. No quality/latency pass is claimed before measurement.
Every evaluation records code commit, dataset hash, method/model revision, prompt/config and environment. Non-deterministic methods report settings and run variability.
Successful writes are durable across an app restart. Review changes preserve raw outputs. A backup/restore rehearsal reconciles customer, interaction and review counts.
API rejects interaction text above 2,000 words or 100 KB and imports above 100 records. Client rendering treats transcript/model output as text, not executable HTML.
Only a human action sets approval. An algorithmic confidence value is not presented as a probability of correctness unless calibrated.
